detailed_description: Encoding Detector checks pasted text or one selected file in the browser and reports likely encodings from simple byte-pattern checks. It detects common byte order marks for UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, and UTF-32 LE/BE, checks whether the bytes form valid UTF-8, identifies all-ASCII input, and falls back to ISO-8859-1 when the bytes are not valid UTF-8. Results show the detected encoding, a confidence percentage, and a short detail message. It does not use machine learning, deep statistical language models, drag-and-drop upload, hundreds of code pages, candidate dropdowns, or downloadable reports.
usage_steps: Paste text into the textarea and click Analyze Text to check the encoded bytes produced by the browser.
Or click Upload File and choose one local file to analyze its raw bytes.
Review the file name and size when a file is selected.
Read each detected encoding result with its confidence percentage and detail message.
Use the results as a lightweight hint for UTF and ASCII style encoding issues.
usage_examples: Check whether a pasted snippet is plain ASCII or valid UTF-8.
Inspect a small text file for a UTF-8 or UTF-16 byte order mark.
Confirm that a file with garbled characters is not being recognized as valid UTF-8.
Use the confidence and detail text as a quick browser-side diagnostic before trying a dedicated encoding library.

faqs.question: Is the Encoding Detector free?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is completely free with no signup, and you can analyze as much text or as many files as you need.

faqs.question: Which encodings can it detect?
faqs.answer: It detects UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, UTF-32 LE/BE byte order marks, checks whether bytes form valid UTF-8, identifies all-ASCII input, and falls back to ISO-8859-1 when nothing else matches.

faqs.question: Is my text or file uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Byte-pattern analysis runs locally in your browser — neither pasted text nor selected files are sent to any server.

faqs.question: Why does detection sometimes return ISO-8859-1?
faqs.answer: When no BOM is present and the bytes are not valid UTF-8, ISO-8859-1 is used as a permissive fallback because it accepts any byte sequence.

faqs.question: Can it detect encodings like GBK or Shift-JIS?
faqs.answer: No. The detector focuses on Unicode family encodings and ASCII. For East Asian multi-byte encodings, specialized tools are required.
